name: Podiatry
tagline: Foot care, orthotics, ingrown nails, diabetes care

emergency: red or hot foot with fever

extra_prompt: You are booking for a podiatry clinic. Ask about the foot concern, medical history (especially diabetes), current footwear, and pain level. Ask whether they need orthotics or nail surgery. Quote prices only from the reference answers, and say the final price is confirmed after assessment. Do not provide clinical advice or promise specific treatment outcomes.

kb.q: How much does a visit cost?
kb.a: {price_note} Initial and follow-up consultations are priced separately. We confirm the fee before you book.

kb.q: Can I claim on private health?
kb.a: Yes, if you have podiatry cover with your health fund. We offer HICAPS claiming where available, so ask us at booking.
Yes, we offer custom and prefabricated orthotics. Custom orthotics are made after an assessment, and prefabricated orthotics can be fitted at a visit.
Yes, we treat ingrown nails, including partial nail avulsion (PNA) where needed. We explain the options and get your consent before any procedure.

kb.q: Do you do diabetic foot care?
kb.a: Yes, we offer diabetic foot assessments and ulcer care. Please tell us at booking if you have diabetes, as it changes how we assess your feet.
Yes, we treat fungal nails with laser and topical treatments. Results vary, so we discuss the likely timeframe at your assessment.
Yes, we treat warts with cryotherapy and needling. We explain the options and the likely number of sessions before treatment starts.
Yes, we treat heel pain, including plantar fasciitis. We look at your footwear and gait as part of the plan.
Yes, partial nail avulsion (PNA) and total nail avulsion are available. We discuss the procedure, aftercare and consent with you before booking.
Yes, paediatric podiatry is available for children. Please bring a parent or guardian to the appointment.
Yes, we offer sports podiatry, including biomechanical and gait analysis. Tell us your sport and how often you train.
Yes, home visits are available in the local metro area. Ask us to confirm your suburb, and we confirm the home visit fee at booking.
Yes, telehealth is available for advice and some follow-up visits. Hands-on assessments and treatment need an in-person visit.
Initial visits are 45 to 60 minutes. Follow-up visits are 30 minutes.
No referral is needed for private podiatry. Some plans, such as Medicare EPC, need a GP referral, so check your plan first.
Cancelling with less than {cancellation_notice} may incur a fee. Please let us know as early as you can.
Our podiatrists hold [registration number] and [insurance details]. Ask us for copies before you book.

templates.reminder: Reminder: your {job} at {business} is on {date}. Please bring your card and any referral.
templates.quote_intro: Here is your estimate. Your practitioner will confirm the plan at your appointment.
templates.invoice_note: Thank you. Health fund claims are handled by the practice where applicable.

required_information.label: Referral or Medicare details (only if the practice needs them)
Clinical details stay in the clinical record, not in booking notes

compliance.guidance: Health practitioners usually need registration (for example with AHPRA where it applies) and current professional indemnity insurance. Keep clinical details in the clinical record, not in general booking fields. Follow your state health privacy rules.
items: Clinical notes kept only in the clinical record
